questions.q: What launched Phil Knight's shoe business?
a: A cold call that won him US distribution rights
A loan from a college running coach
A retail store he opened with friends
A shoe design he built in his garage
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Knight cold-called Onitsuka and left with rights for the western US.

questions.q: How did Knight choose the name Blue Ribbon?
a: He blurted it out when asked for a company name
He named it after his college track team
He took it from his first shoe model
His partner suggested it over dinner
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he improvised the name when Onitsuka asked.

questions.q: What did Bill Bowerman offer Knight?
a: To become his partner and take charge of design
To lend him money for a factory
To coach him for the Olympics
To sell shoes on the East Coast
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Bowerman offered to partner and handle product design.

questions.q: How did Bowerman work on improving shoes?
a: He took them apart and rebuilt them with new materials
He tested them only on Olympic athletes
He ordered lighter soles from Germany
He copied the designs of rival brands
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes Bowerman tearing shoes apart and rebuilding them.

questions.q: What management style does the summary praise?
a: Tell people the result you want and let them find the how
Give detailed instructions for every single task
Promote managers only from outside the firm
Keep all decisions inside a small circle
questions.why: Lesson 3 credits Knight's hands-off style with letting strong people do their thing.
